title: Oklahoma's 768 Rushing Yards Against Kansas State in 1988
question: How many rushing yards did Oklahoma gain against Kansas State in 1988?
answer: Oklahoma rushed for 768 yards on 72 carries in a 70-24 win over Kansas State on October 15, 1988, in Norman. It was the NCAA single-game rushing record for a team until Davidson of the FCS ran for 789 yards in 2018.
summary: On Oct. 15, 1988, Oklahoma ran for 768 yards in a 70-24 win over Kansas State, a team rushing record that lasted three decades. Here is the story.
body: Oklahoma's wishbone offense has produced plenty of gaudy numbers, but none larger than the afternoon of October 15, 1988, at Owen Field. The Sooners beat Kansas State 70-24 and ran for 768 yards on 72 carries, an average of nearly 11 yards every time they handed off or kept the ball.

The box score shows how evenly the load was spread. Eric Mitchel carried six times for 161 yards and two touchdowns, quarterback Charles Thompson ran ten times for 123 yards and three touchdowns, and Mike Gaddis added 55 yards and a score on just three carries. Oklahoma finished with 829 total yards to Kansas State's 419, and the Wildcats managed only 72 yards on the ground.
The run-heavy plan was almost total: by one account the Sooners ran 72 of their 86 plays on the ground. That fit the team Barry Switzer's staff had built, an option attack that wore opponents down.

The 768 yards went into the NCAA record book as the most rushing yards by a team in a single game, and it stood for 30 years. In November 2018, Davidson ran for 789 yards in a 56-52 loss at San Diego, which passed Oklahoma's mark as the Division I record. Oklahoma's total is still cited as a school and FBS-level standard, and it remains one of the program's signature offensive afternoons.
